newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebel leader meets Kenyan president's envoy.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader meets Kenyan president's envoy.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Friday held talks with special envoy of Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi at rebel headquarters in the southeastern city of Lubumbashi, Kenyan and rebel sources said.
Lonrho East Africa Chairman Mark Too delivered Moi's message at a two-hour meeting with the Zairean rebel leader.
Details of the message were not immediately known but Kabila spoke to Moi by telephone soon after, Kenyan sources said.

It was the first contact between Kabila and Moi since Kabila launched his drive to push Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko out of office last October. Moi and Mobutu, who has ruled Zaire for 32 years, were known to be friends.
Kabila was expected to visit the Kenyan capital in the coming days, according to his "foreign minister" Bizima Karaha.

Karaha said Moi was an elder statesman who had a definite role to play in ending the Zairean crisis. Kenyan officials saw that as a major step forward because Kabila had previously refused to come to Nairobi saying Moi was too close to Mobutu.
Diplomats said Kabila saw Moi as having been instrumental in ending the civil war in Mozambique.
Moi has chaired two lots of peace talks on Zaire, culminating in a special Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit on the Zairean crisis in Lome, Togo, last month.
Kabila's biggest regional support is seen as coming from Uganda and Rwanda, according to regional diplomats.
